# =============================================================
# Agri LMS — Module Model
# =============================================================
# File    : app/models/module.py
# Purpose : Defines the Module database model representing
#           individual learning units within a Course.
#
#           A Module is the second level of the learning
#           hierarchy. Each course contains one or more
#           modules arranged in a strict sequential order.
#           Learners must complete each module before
#           unlocking the next one.
#
#           The admin specifies which module is the final
#           module in a course using the is_last_module flag.
#           This flag is what the system uses to determine
#           when a learner has completed an entire course.
#
# Relationships:
#   Module >── Course       (many modules belong to one course)
#   Module ──< Material     (one module has many materials)
#   Module ──< Progress     (one module has many progress records)
#
# Learning Hierarchy:
#   Course
#     └── Module 1  (order_number=1)
#           └── Material (video)
#           └── Material (PDF)
#     └── Module 2  (order_number=2)
#           └── Material (video)
#     └── Module N  (order_number=N, is_last_module=True)
#           └── Material
# =============================================================

from datetime import datetime
from app.extensions import db


# =============================================================
# MODULE MODEL
# =============================================================

class Module(db.Model):
    """
    Represents a single learning module within a Course.

    Modules are the core content delivery unit of the platform.
    Each module has an order number that determines its position
    in the course sequence. Learners progress through modules
    one at a time in ascending order_number sequence.

    The admin sets is_last_module=True on exactly one module
    per course to indicate where the course ends. The system
    uses this flag — not a count — to determine completion,
    giving the admin full flexibility to add or remove modules
    without reconfiguring the course structure.

    Each module contains one or more Materials (videos, PDFs,
    documents) that the learner consumes before marking the
    module as complete and moving to the next.
    """

    __tablename__ = 'modules'

    # ── Table-level constraints ───────────────────────────────
    __table_args__ = (
        # Enforce unique ordering within each course
        # No two modules in the same course can share an order number
        db.UniqueConstraint(
            'course_id',
            'order_number',
            name='uq_module_course_order'
        ),
    )

    # ── Primary Key ───────────────────────────────────────────
    id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        primary_key=True,
        autoincrement=True,
        comment='Unique module identifier — auto-incremented primary key'
    )

    # ── Foreign Key — Parent Course ───────────────────────────
    course_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('courses.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the course this module belongs to. '
            'CASCADE: deleting a course deletes all its modules.'
        )
    )

    # ── Module Identity ───────────────────────────────────────
    title = db.Column(
        db.String(300),
        nullable=False,
        comment='Title of the module displayed to learners — e.g. Module 1: Introduction to Soil Types'
    )

    description = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment='Overview of what this module covers — shown before the learner starts'
    )

    learning_objectives = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Newline-separated list of specific things the learner '
            'will be able to do after completing this module'
        )
    )

    # ── Sequencing ────────────────────────────────────────────
    order_number = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=False,
        comment=(
            'Position of this module in the course sequence. '
            'Module 1 has order_number=1, Module 2 has order_number=2, etc. '
            'Learners progress through modules in ascending order. '
            'Must be unique within a course — enforced by uq_module_course_order.'
        )
    )

    # ── Last Module Flag ──────────────────────────────────────
    is_last_module = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Designates this module as the final module of the course. '
            'Set by the admin when creating or editing the module. '
            'When a learner completes a module where is_last_module=True, '
            'the system automatically marks their course enrollment as complete. '
            'Only one module per course should have this set to True.'
        )
    )

    # ── Estimated Duration ────────────────────────────────────
    duration_minutes = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=True,
        comment='Estimated time in minutes a learner needs to complete this module'
    )

    # ── Content Notes ─────────────────────────────────────────
    notes = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Supplementary notes, key takeaways, or additional reading '
            'written by the admin — displayed alongside the materials'
        )
    )

    instructor_notes = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Internal admin-only notes about this module — '
            'not visible to learners'
        )
    )

    # ── Publishing Status ─────────────────────────────────────
    is_published = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Publication flag — '
            'False: module is a draft, visible only to admins | '
            'True: module is visible to enrolled learners'
        )
    )

    # ── Free Preview ──────────────────────────────────────────
    is_free_preview = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Preview flag — '
            'True: this module is accessible to non-enrolled users '
            'as a sample before they enroll in the course'
        )
    )

    # ── Timestamps ────────────────────────────────────────────
    date_created = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=False,
        default=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of when this module was created by the admin'
    )

    date_updated = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=True,
        onupdate=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of the most recent update to this module'
    )

    # ── Relationships ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # One module contains many materials
    # Ordered by the material's own order_number for display
    materials = db.relationship(
        'Material',
        backref='module',
        lazy='dynamic',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan',
        order_by='Material.order_number'
    )

    # One module has many learner progress records
    # One record per learner per module
    progress_records = db.relationship(
        'Progress',
        backref='module',
        lazy='dynamic',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # MATERIAL HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_all_materials(self):
        """
        Retrieve all materials in this module including
        unpublished drafts. Used by admin views.

        Returns:
            list[Material]: All materials ordered by order_number.
        """
        from app.models.material import Material
        return self.materials.order_by(
            Material.order_number
        ).all()

    def get_published_materials(self):
        """
        Retrieve only published materials in this module.
        Used by learner views.

        Returns:
            list[Material]: Published materials ordered by order_number.
        """
        from app.models.material import Material
        return self.materials.filter_by(
            is_published=True
        ).order_by(Material.order_number).all()

    def get_materials_by_type(self, material_type):
        """
        Retrieve all published materials of a specific type
        in this module.

        Args:
            material_type (str): The type to filter by.
                                 Options: 'video' | 'pdf' |
                                 'document' | 'image' | 'other'

        Returns:
            list[Material]: Filtered and ordered materials.
        """
        from app.models.material import Material
        return self.materials.filter_by(
            material_type=material_type,
            is_published=True
        ).order_by(Material.order_number).all()

    def get_video_count(self):
        """
        Count the number of video materials in this module.

        Returns:
            int: Number of video materials.
        """
        return self.materials.filter_by(
            material_type='video',
            is_published=True
        ).count()

    def get_pdf_count(self):
        """
        Count the number of PDF materials in this module.

        Returns:
            int: Number of PDF materials.
        """
        return self.materials.filter_by(
            material_type='pdf',
            is_published=True
        ).count()

    def get_total_materials_count(self):
        """
        Count all materials in this module regardless of type
        or publishing status. Used in admin views.

        Returns:
            int: Total material count.
        """
        return self.materials.count()

    def get_published_materials_count(self):
        """
        Count only published materials in this module.

        Returns:
            int: Published material count.
        """
        return self.materials.filter_by(
            is_published=True
        ).count()

    # ==========================================================
    # SEQUENCING HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_next_module(self):
        """
        Retrieve the next module in the course sequence.
        Returns None if this is already the last module.

        Returns:
            Module or None: The next module in sequence.
        """
        return Module.query.filter(
            Module.course_id == self.course_id,
            Module.order_number > self.order_number,
            Module.is_published == True
        ).order_by(Module.order_number).first()

    def get_previous_module(self):
        """
        Retrieve the previous module in the course sequence.
        Returns None if this is the first module.

        Returns:
            Module or None: The previous module in sequence.
        """
        return Module.query.filter(
            Module.course_id == self.course_id,
            Module.order_number < self.order_number,
            Module.is_published == True
        ).order_by(Module.order_number.desc()).first()

    def is_first_module(self):
        """
        Determine whether this is the first module in its course
        by checking if no module with a lower order_number exists.

        Returns:
            bool: True if this is the first module.
        """
        return Module.query.filter(
            Module.course_id == self.course_id,
            Module.order_number < self.order_number
        ).count() == 0

    # ==========================================================
    # PROGRESS HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_completion_count(self):
        """
        Count how many learners have completed this module.

        Returns:
            int: Number of learners who completed this module.
        """
        from app.models.progress import Progress
        return self.progress_records.filter_by(
            is_completed=True
        ).count()

    def is_completed_by(self, user_id):
        """
        Check whether a specific learner has completed
        this module.

        Args:
            user_id (int): The primary key of the learner.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the learner has completed this module.
        """
        from app.models.progress import Progress
        record = self.progress_records.filter_by(
            user_id=user_id,
            is_completed=True
        ).first()
        return record is not None

    def get_progress_for_user(self, user_id):
        """
        Retrieve the Progress record for a specific learner
        on this module.

        Args:
            user_id (int): The primary key of the learner.

        Returns:
            Progress or None: The progress record if it exists.
        """
        from app.models.progress import Progress
        return self.progress_records.filter_by(
            user_id=user_id
        ).first()

    # ==========================================================
    # CONTENT HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_learning_objectives_list(self):
        """
        Parse the newline-separated learning objectives text
        into a clean Python list for template rendering.

        Returns:
            list[str]: List of individual objective strings.
                       Returns empty list if none are set.

        Example:
            'Identify soil types\\nTest soil pH\\nApply amendments'
            → ['Identify soil types', 'Test soil pH', 'Apply amendments']
        """
        if not self.learning_objectives:
            return []
        return [
            obj.strip()
            for obj in self.learning_objectives.splitlines()
            if obj.strip()
        ]

    def get_duration_display(self):
        """
        Format the duration_minutes value into a
        human-readable hours and minutes string.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted duration string.

        Examples:
            45  → '45 min'
            90  → '1 hr 30 min'
            120 → '2 hr'
        """
        if not self.duration_minutes:
            return 'N/A'

        minutes = self.duration_minutes

        if minutes < 60:
            return f'{minutes} min'

        hours = minutes // 60
        remaining_minutes = minutes % 60

        if remaining_minutes == 0:
            return f'{hours} hr'

        return f'{hours} hr {remaining_minutes} min'

    def get_module_label(self):
        """
        Generate a formatted module label combining the
        order number and title for display in navigation
        and breadcrumbs.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted label string.

        Example:
            order_number=3, title='Soil pH Testing'
            → 'Module 3: Soil pH Testing'
        """
        return f'Module {self.order_number}: {self.title}'

    # ==========================================================
    # SERIALIZATION
    # ==========================================================

    def to_dict(self, include_materials=False):
        """
        Serialize the Module object to a plain dictionary.

        Args:
            include_materials (bool): If True, includes a
                serialized list of all published materials.
                Default is False for performance.

        Returns:
            dict: Module data with optional materials included.
        """
        data = {
            'id':                       self.id,
            'course_id':                self.course_id,
            'title':                    self.title,
            'description':              self.description,
            'learning_objectives':      self.get_learning_objectives_list(),
            'order_number':             self.order_number,
            'is_last_module':           self.is_last_module,
            'duration_minutes':         self.duration_minutes,
            'duration_display':         self.get_duration_display(),
            'module_label':             self.get_module_label(),
            'notes':                    self.notes,
            'is_published':             self.is_published,
            'is_free_preview':          self.is_free_preview,
            'is_first_module':          self.is_first_module(),
            'total_materials':          self.get_total_materials_count(),
            'published_materials':      self.get_published_materials_count(),
            'video_count':              self.get_video_count(),
            'pdf_count':                self.get_pdf_count(),
            'completion_count':         self.get_completion_count(),
            'date_created':             self.date_created.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            'date_updated':             self.date_updated.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
                                        if self.date_updated else None,
        }

        # Optionally include serialized materials
        if include_materials:
            data['materials'] = [
                material.to_dict()
                for material in self.get_published_materials()
            ]

        return data

    # ==========================================================
    # STRING REPRESENTATION
    # ==========================================================

    def __repr__(self):
        return (
            f'<Module id={self.id} '
            f'course_id={self.course_id} '
            f'order={self.order_number} '
            f'title={self.title!r} '
            f'last={self.is_last_module}>'
        )

# =============================================================
# Agri LMS — Progress Model
# =============================================================
# File    : app/models/progress.py
# Purpose : Defines the Progress database model representing
#           a single learner's completion record for a single
#           module within a course they are enrolled in.
#
#           Progress is tracked at the module level — one
#           Progress record exists per learner per module.
#           When a learner opens a module and marks it as
#           complete, a Progress record is created or updated.
#
#           The collection of Progress records for a learner
#           across all modules in a course is used to:
#               1. Calculate enrollment.progress_percent
#               2. Determine which module to unlock next
#               3. Detect when the last module is complete
#                  and trigger course completion
#               4. Display a visual progress timeline
#                  to the learner on their dashboard
#
#           A learner can only mark a module complete if
#           they have completed all previous modules first —
#           enforced in the route handler logic, not the model.
#
# Relationships:
#   Progress >── User     (many progress records per learner)
#   Progress >── Module   (many progress records per module)
#
# Progress Lifecycle:
#   Learner clicks on a module
#       → Progress record created (is_completed=False)
#         if one does not already exist — tracking started
#       → Learner consumes module materials
#       → Learner clicks "Mark as Complete"
#       → Progress.mark_complete() called
#       → is_completed=True, date_completed recorded
#       → Enrollment.modules_completed incremented
#       → Enrollment.progress_percent recalculated
#       → If module.is_last_module=True:
#             Enrollment.mark_completed() triggered
#             Course completion flow begins
# =============================================================

from datetime import datetime
from app.extensions import db


# =============================================================
# PROGRESS MODEL
# =============================================================

class Progress(db.Model):
    """
    Represents a single learner's interaction and completion
    record for a single module within an enrolled course.

    One Progress record exists per learner per module.
    This is enforced by the uq_progress_user_module
    unique constraint on (user_id, module_id).

    The model tracks:
        - Whether the learner has started the module
          (record exists)
        - Whether the learner has completed the module
          (is_completed=True)
        - When they first accessed the module
          (date_started)
        - When they marked it complete
          (date_completed)
        - How long they spent on the module
          (time_spent_minutes)
        - Their last access timestamp
          (last_accessed)
        - Optional self-assessment notes
          (learner_notes)
    """

    __tablename__ = 'progress'

    # ── Table-level constraints ───────────────────────────────
    __table_args__ = (
        # One progress record per learner per module
        db.UniqueConstraint(
            'user_id',
            'module_id',
            name='uq_progress_user_module'
        ),
    )

    # ── Primary Key ───────────────────────────────────────────
    id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        primary_key=True,
        autoincrement=True,
        comment='Unique progress record identifier — auto-incremented primary key'
    )

    # ── Foreign Keys ──────────────────────────────────────────
    user_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('users.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the learner this progress '
            'record belongs to. '
            'CASCADE: deleting a user removes all their progress records.'
        )
    )

    module_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('modules.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the module this progress '
            'record tracks. '
            'CASCADE: deleting a module removes all its progress records.'
        )
    )

    # ── Convenience Foreign Key ───────────────────────────────
    # Stored for fast filtering of all progress records
    # for a learner within a specific course without
    # needing to join through the modules table
    course_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('courses.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the course this module belongs to. '
            'Stored as a convenience to allow fast filtering of '
            'all progress records for a learner in a course '
            'without joining through the modules table. '
            'CASCADE: deleting a course removes all related progress.'
        )
    )

    # ── Completion Status ─────────────────────────────────────
    is_completed = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Module completion flag. '
            'False: learner has started but not yet completed this module. '
            'True: learner has explicitly marked this module as complete.'
        )
    )

    # ── Time Tracking ─────────────────────────────────────────
    date_started = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=False,
        default=datetime.utcnow,
        comment=(
            'UTC timestamp of when the learner first opened '
            'this module — the moment the Progress record was created.'
        )
    )

    date_completed = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'UTC timestamp of when the learner clicked '
            '"Mark as Complete" and is_completed was set to True.'
        )
    )

    last_accessed = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=False,
        default=datetime.utcnow,
        comment=(
            'UTC timestamp of the most recent time the learner '
            'opened this module. Updated every time the learner '
            'visits the module view page.'
        )
    )

    time_spent_minutes = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=False,
        default=0,
        comment=(
            'Cumulative number of minutes the learner has spent '
            'on this module across all visits. '
            'Incremented each time the learner leaves the module '
            'page — tracked via JavaScript session timing '
            'and submitted with the page-leave event.'
        )
    )

    # ── Access Count ──────────────────────────────────────────
    access_count = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=False,
        default=1,
        comment=(
            'Number of times the learner has opened this module. '
            'Incremented on each visit to the module view page. '
            'Starts at 1 when the Progress record is created '
            'on the first visit.'
        )
    )

    # ── Learner Self-Assessment ───────────────────────────────
    learner_notes = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Optional personal notes the learner writes while '
            'studying this module. Private to the learner — '
            'not visible to admins. Displayed in the module '
            'view as a personal notepad.'
        )
    )

    learner_rating = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Optional learner satisfaction rating for this module '
            'on a scale of 1 to 5. '
            '1=Very Poor, 2=Poor, 3=Fair, 4=Good, 5=Excellent. '
            'Used for admin analytics and course improvement.'
        )
    )

    learner_feedback = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Optional written feedback the learner submits '
            'about this module after completing it. '
            'Visible to admins for course improvement purposes.'
        )
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # COMPLETION METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def mark_complete(self):
        """
        Mark this module as completed by the learner.

        Sets is_completed to True and records the
        completion timestamp.

        This method does NOT automatically update the
        parent Enrollment record — that is handled in
        the route handler to keep the model focused
        on its own data and avoid circular logic.

        After calling this method, the route handler
        should:
            1. Call enrollment.increment_modules_completed()
            2. Call enrollment.update_progress(total_modules)
            3. Check if module.is_last_module is True
            4. If so, call enrollment.mark_completed()
        """
        self.is_completed = True
        self.date_completed = datetime.utcnow()

    def mark_incomplete(self):
        """
        Revert this module's completion status back to
        incomplete. Used by admins to reset a learner's
        progress on a specific module if needed.

        Clears is_completed and date_completed.
        """
        self.is_completed = False
        self.date_completed = None

    # ==========================================================
    # ACCESS TRACKING METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def record_access(self):
        """
        Record a new access event for this module.

        Increments the access_count and updates the
        last_accessed timestamp to the current UTC time.

        Should be called every time a learner opens
        the module view page.
        """
        self.access_count += 1
        self.last_accessed = datetime.utcnow()

    def add_time_spent(self, minutes):
        """
        Add to the cumulative time the learner has spent
        on this module.

        Args:
            minutes (int): Number of minutes to add.
                           Should come from JavaScript
                           session timing submitted when
                           the learner leaves the page.
                           Negative values are ignored.
        """
        if minutes and minutes > 0:
            self.time_spent_minutes += int(minutes)

    # ==========================================================
    # LEARNER FEEDBACK METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def save_rating_and_feedback(self, rating, feedback=None):
        """
        Save the learner's satisfaction rating and optional
        written feedback for this module.

        Args:
            rating (int): Satisfaction rating between 1 and 5.
                          Values outside this range are clamped.
            feedback (str, optional): Written feedback text.
        """
        # Clamp rating to valid range
        if rating is not None:
            self.learner_rating = max(1, min(5, int(rating)))

        if feedback and feedback.strip():
            self.learner_feedback = feedback.strip()

    def save_notes(self, notes):
        """
        Save or update the learner's personal study notes
        for this module.

        Args:
            notes (str): The learner's note content.
                         Pass an empty string to clear notes.
        """
        self.learner_notes = notes.strip() if notes else None

    # ==========================================================
    # TIME DISPLAY HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_time_spent_display(self):
        """
        Format the cumulative time_spent_minutes into a
        human-readable hours and minutes string.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted time string.

        Examples:
            0   → 'Less than a minute'
            45  → '45 min'
            90  → '1 hr 30 min'
            120 → '2 hr'
        """
        minutes = self.time_spent_minutes

        if minutes <= 0:
            return 'Less than a minute'
        elif minutes < 60:
            return f'{minutes} min'

        hours = minutes // 60
        remaining = minutes % 60

        if remaining == 0:
            return f'{hours} hr'
        return f'{hours} hr {remaining} min'

    def get_days_to_complete(self):
        """
        Calculate the number of days it took the learner
        to complete this module from first access to
        marking it complete.

        Returns:
            int or None: Days taken to complete.
                         None if the module is not yet complete.
        """
        if self.is_completed and self.date_completed:
            delta = self.date_completed - self.date_started
            return max(delta.days, 0)
        return None

    def get_days_since_start(self):
        """
        Calculate the number of days since the learner
        first opened this module.

        Returns:
            int: Days since first access.
        """
        delta = datetime.utcnow() - self.date_started
        return delta.days

    def get_last_accessed_display(self):
        """
        Format the last_accessed timestamp into a
        human-readable string for display in templates.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted last access date string.

        Example:
            '15 January 2025 at 02:30 PM UTC'
        """
        return self.last_accessed.strftime('%d %B %Y at %I:%M %p UTC')

    def get_date_completed_display(self):
        """
        Format the date_completed timestamp into a
        human-readable string for display.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted completion date or 'Not completed yet'.
        """
        if not self.date_completed:
            return 'Not completed yet'
        return self.date_completed.strftime('%d %B %Y at %I:%M %p UTC')

    # ==========================================================
    # RATING HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_rating_display(self):
        """
        Return a human-readable label for the learner's
        module satisfaction rating.

        Returns:
            str: Descriptive rating label.
        """
        labels = {
            1: 'Very Poor',
            2: 'Poor',
            3: 'Fair',
            4: 'Good',
            5: 'Excellent',
        }
        return labels.get(self.learner_rating, 'Not rated')

    def get_rating_stars(self):
        """
        Return a star string representation of the learner's
        rating for visual display in templates.

        Returns:
            str: Star characters representing the rating.

        Examples:
            rating=5 → '★★★★★'
            rating=3 → '★★★☆☆'
            None     → '☆☆☆☆☆'
        """
        if not self.learner_rating:
            return '☆☆☆☆☆'
        filled = '★' * self.learner_rating
        empty = '☆' * (5 - self.learner_rating)
        return filled + empty

    # ==========================================================
    # STATIC FACTORY METHOD
    # ==========================================================

    @staticmethod
    def get_or_create(user_id, module_id, course_id):
        """
        Retrieve the existing Progress record for a learner
        and module, or create a new one if it does not exist.

        This is the standard way to ensure a Progress record
        exists when a learner opens a module for the first
        time. On subsequent visits, the existing record is
        returned and record_access() is called on it.

        Args:
            user_id (int): The learner's primary key.
            module_id (int): The module's primary key.
            course_id (int): The course's primary key.

        Returns:
            tuple: (Progress, bool) where the bool is True
                   if the record was newly created,
                   False if it already existed.

        Usage in route handler:
            progress, created = Progress.get_or_create(
                user_id=current_user.id,
                module_id=module.id,
                course_id=module.course_id
            )
            if not created:
                progress.record_access()
            db.session.commit()
        """
        existing = Progress.query.filter_by(
            user_id=user_id,
            module_id=module_id
        ).first()

        if existing:
            return existing, False

        # Create a new progress record
        new_progress = Progress(
            user_id=user_id,
            module_id=module_id,
            course_id=course_id,
            is_completed=False,
            date_started=datetime.utcnow(),
            last_accessed=datetime.utcnow(),
            access_count=1,
            time_spent_minutes=0
        )
        db.session.add(new_progress)

        return new_progress, True

    @staticmethod
    def get_course_progress_for_user(user_id, course_id):
        """
        Retrieve all Progress records for a specific learner
        within a specific course, ordered by module sequence.

        Used to render the course progress timeline on the
        learner dashboard and course detail page.

        Args:
            user_id (int): The learner's primary key.
            course_id (int): The course's primary key.

        Returns:
            list[Progress]: Ordered list of progress records.
        """
        from app.models.module import Module
        return (
            Progress.query
            .join(Module, Progress.module_id == Module.id)
            .filter(
                Progress.user_id == user_id,
                Progress.course_id == course_id
            )
            .order_by(Module.order_number)
            .all()
        )

    @staticmethod
    def count_completed_for_user_in_course(user_id, course_id):
        """
        Count how many modules a learner has completed
        in a specific course.

        Used to verify the enrollment.modules_completed
        count and for recalculation if needed.

        Args:
            user_id (int): The learner's primary key.
            course_id (int): The course's primary key.

        Returns:
            int: Number of completed modules.
        """
        return Progress.query.filter_by(
            user_id=user_id,
            course_id=course_id,
            is_completed=True
        ).count()

    # ==========================================================
    # SERIALIZATION
    # ==========================================================

    def to_dict(self):
        """
        Serialize the Progress object to a plain dictionary
        suitable for JSON responses and template rendering.

        Returns:
            dict: Progress data with all computed fields.
        """
        return {
            'id':                       self.id,
            'user_id':                  self.user_id,
            'module_id':                self.module_id,
            'course_id':                self.course_id,
            'is_completed':             self.is_completed,
            'date_started':             self.date_started.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            'date_completed':           self.date_completed.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
                                        if self.date_completed else None,
            'date_completed_display':   self.get_date_completed_display(),
            'last_accessed':            self.last_accessed.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            'last_accessed_display':    self.get_last_accessed_display(),
            'time_spent_minutes':       self.time_spent_minutes,
            'time_spent_display':       self.get_time_spent_display(),
            'access_count':             self.access_count,
            'days_to_complete':         self.get_days_to_complete(),
            'days_since_start':         self.get_days_since_start(),
            'learner_notes':            self.learner_notes,
            'learner_rating':           self.learner_rating,
            'rating_display':           self.get_rating_display(),
            'rating_stars':             self.get_rating_stars(),
            'learner_feedback':         self.learner_feedback,
        }

    # ==========================================================
    # STRING REPRESENTATION
    # ==========================================================

    def __repr__(self):
        return (
            f'<Progress id={self.id} '
            f'user_id={self.user_id} '
            f'module_id={self.module_id} '
            f'completed={self.is_completed} '
            f'time={self.time_spent_minutes}min>'
        )

FILE: .\app\models\submission.py

# =============================================================
# Agri LMS — Submission Model
# =============================================================
# File    : app/models/submission.py
# Purpose : Defines the Submission database model representing
#           a learner's response to an assignment.
#
#           A Submission is created when a learner submits
#           their work for an assignment. Depending on the
#           assignment's submission_type, a submission can
#           contain:
#               - A typed text response (text_content field)
#               - An uploaded file (file_name, stored_file_name)
#               - Both a typed response and an uploaded file
#
#           Each submission has a status that tracks its
#           lifecycle from the moment it is submitted through
#           to when it is graded and the learner is notified.
#
#           The Grade model is a separate linked record
#           created by the admin when grading a submission.
#           The Submission model itself holds a convenience
#           is_graded flag and a score_percent field that
#           are updated when a Grade record is saved, to
#           make querying and display faster without always
#           joining to the Grade table.
#
# Relationships:
#   Submission >── User         (many submissions by one learner)
#   Submission >── Assignment   (many submissions for one assignment)
#   Submission ──< Grade        (one submission has one grade)
#
# Submission Lifecycle:
#   Learner opens assignment page
#       → Learner types text and/or uploads file
#       → Learner clicks Submit
#       → Submission record created (status='submitted')
#       → Admin sees submission in grading queue
#       → Admin opens submission, reviews content
#       → Admin awards score and writes feedback
#       → Grade record created
#       → Submission updated (is_graded=True, status='graded')
#       → Learner sees grade and feedback on their submission page
# =============================================================

from datetime import datetime
from app.extensions import db


# =============================================================
# SUBMISSION STATUS CONSTANTS
# =============================================================

SUBMISSION_STATUS_SUBMITTED = 'submitted'   # Awaiting admin review
SUBMISSION_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW = 'under_review'  # Admin is reviewing
SUBMISSION_STATUS_GRADED    = 'graded'      # Grade has been assigned
SUBMISSION_STATUS_RETURNED  = 'returned'    # Returned for revision
SUBMISSION_STATUS_LATE      = 'late'        # Submitted after deadline

SUBMISSION_STATUSES = [
    SUBMISSION_STATUS_SUBMITTED,
    SUBMISSION_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW,
    SUBMISSION_STATUS_GRADED,
    SUBMISSION_STATUS_RETURNED,
    SUBMISSION_STATUS_LATE,
]


# =============================================================
# SUBMISSION MODEL
# =============================================================

class Submission(db.Model):
    """
    Represents a single learner submission for an assignment.

    A learner may make multiple submissions for the same
    assignment if the assignment's max_submissions allows it.
    Each submission is a separate record with its own
    content, file, status, and grade.

    The text_content field stores the learner's typed
    response. It supports plain text and can store
    lengthy written answers.

    The file fields store metadata about the uploaded
    file. The actual file is saved on the server at
    static/uploads/submissions/.

    When an admin grades a submission, a Grade record is
    created and linked to this submission via the grade
    relationship. The is_graded and score_percent fields
    on the Submission are then updated as denormalized
    copies for fast querying.
    """

    __tablename__ = 'submissions'

    # ── Primary Key ───────────────────────────────────────────
    id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        primary_key=True,
        autoincrement=True,
        comment='Unique submission identifier — auto-incremented primary key'
    )

    # ── Foreign Keys ──────────────────────────────────────────
    user_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('users.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the learner who made this submission. '
            'CASCADE: deleting a user removes all their submissions.'
        )
    )

    assignment_id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        db.ForeignKey('assignments.id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
        comment=(
            'Foreign key — ID of the assignment this submission responds to. '
            'CASCADE: deleting an assignment removes all its submissions.'
        )
    )

    # ── Submission Attempt Number ─────────────────────────────
    attempt_number = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        nullable=False,
        default=1,
        comment=(
            'Sequential attempt number for this learner on this assignment. '
            'First submission has attempt_number=1. '
            'Each resubmission increments this by one. '
            'Used to display "Attempt 1 of 3" to the learner.'
        )
    )

    # ── Text Content ──────────────────────────────────────────
    text_content = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'The learner typed text response to the assignment. '
            'May be NULL if the learner only uploaded a file. '
            'Stored as plain text — supports lengthy written answers.'
        )
    )

    # ── File Upload Fields ────────────────────────────────────
    file_name = db.Column(
        db.String(255),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Original filename of the uploaded submission file '
            'as provided by the learner — stored for display. '
            'May be NULL if the learner only submitted text.'
        )
    )

    stored_file_name = db.Column(
        db.String(255),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'UUID-prefixed server-side filename for the submission file. '
            'File is stored at static/uploads/submissions/. '
            'Used to construct the download URL.'
        )
    )

    file_extension = db.Column(
        db.String(20),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Lowercase file extension of the uploaded file — '
            'e.g. pdf, docx, png. Used for icon display and '
            'validation in the admin grading view.'
        )
    )

    file_size_bytes = db.Column(
        db.BigInteger,
        nullable=True,
        comment='File size in bytes of the uploaded submission file.'
    )

    mime_type = db.Column(
        db.String(100),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'MIME type of the uploaded submission file — '
            'e.g. application/pdf, image/png, '
            'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document'
        )
    )

    # ── Submission Status ─────────────────────────────────────
    status = db.Column(
        db.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=SUBMISSION_STATUS_SUBMITTED,
        comment=(
            'Current status of this submission. '
            'submitted: received and awaiting admin review | '
            'under_review: admin is currently reviewing | '
            'graded: grade has been assigned by admin | '
            'returned: returned to learner for revision | '
            'late: submitted after the assignment due_date'
        )
    )

    # ── Late Submission Flag ──────────────────────────────────
    is_late = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Flag indicating this submission was made after '
            'the assignment due_date. Set automatically at '
            'submission time by comparing to assignment.due_date.'
        )
    )

    # ── Grading Convenience Fields ────────────────────────────
    # These are denormalized copies of Grade data for fast
    # querying without always joining to the grades table

    is_graded = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Quick flag indicating whether a Grade record exists '
            'for this submission. Updated when the admin saves a grade. '
            'Used for fast filtering in submission lists.'
        )
    )

    score_percent = db.Column(
        db.Numeric(5, 2),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Denormalized copy of the final percentage score '
            'from the linked Grade record. '
            'Updated when the admin saves the grade. '
            'Allows fast score display without joining grades table.'
        )
    )

    # ── Learner Notes ─────────────────────────────────────────
    learner_notes = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Optional notes from the learner submitted alongside '
            'their work — e.g. explanations, clarifications, '
            'or context for the submission.'
        )
    )

    # ── Admin Flags ───────────────────────────────────────────
    is_flagged = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment=(
            'Admin flag — True means the admin has flagged this '
            'submission for special attention — e.g. suspected '
            'plagiarism, incomplete submission, or exceptional work.'
        )
    )

    flag_reason = db.Column(
        db.String(300),
        nullable=True,
        comment=(
            'Reason the admin flagged this submission. '
            'Only visible to admins — not shown to the learner.'
        )
    )

    # ── Timestamps ────────────────────────────────────────────
    date_submitted = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=False,
        default=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of when the learner submitted this work.'
    )

    date_updated = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=True,
        onupdate=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of the most recent update to this submission record.'
    )

    # ── Relationships ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # One submission has at most one grade record
    # uselist=False enforces the one-to-one relationship
    grade = db.relationship(
        'Grade',
        backref='submission',
        uselist=False,
        lazy='joined',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # CONTENT TYPE DETECTION HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def has_text_content(self):
        """
        Check whether this submission contains a typed
        text response from the learner.

        Returns:
            bool: True if text_content is not empty.
        """
        return bool(self.text_content and self.text_content.strip())

    def has_file(self):
        """
        Check whether this submission contains an uploaded
        file from the learner.

        Returns:
            bool: True if a stored file exists for this submission.
        """
        return bool(self.stored_file_name)

    def has_both(self):
        """
        Check whether this submission contains both a typed
        text response and an uploaded file.

        Returns:
            bool: True if both text and file are present.
        """
        return self.has_text_content() and self.has_file()

    def is_empty(self):
        """
        Check whether this submission contains neither
        text content nor an uploaded file.
        An empty submission should not normally occur
        due to frontend and backend validation.

        Returns:
            bool: True if neither text nor file is present.
        """
        return not self.has_text_content() and not self.has_file()

    # ==========================================================
    # FILE HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_file_url(self):
        """
        Build the relative URL path for downloading or
        viewing the submitted file through Flask's
        static file serving route.

        Returns:
            str or None: Relative URL path to the submission file.
                         None if no file was uploaded.

        Example:
            'uploads/submissions/a3f1c2d4_assignment1_report.pdf'
        """
        if self.stored_file_name:
            return f'uploads/submissions/{self.stored_file_name}'
        return None

    def get_file_size_display(self):
        """
        Convert raw file_size_bytes into a human-readable
        string with the appropriate unit suffix.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted file size or 'Unknown size'.

        Examples:
            1024       → '1.0 KB'
            2097152    → '2.0 MB'
        """
        if not self.file_size_bytes:
            return 'Unknown size'

        size = self.file_size_bytes
        if size < 1024:
            return f'{size} B'
        elif size < 1024 ** 2:
            return f'{size / 1024:.1f} KB'
        elif size < 1024 ** 3:
            return f'{size / (1024 ** 2):.1f} MB'
        else:
            return f'{size / (1024 ** 3):.1f} GB'

    def get_file_icon(self):
        """
        Return an emoji icon string for the uploaded file
        based on its extension, for use in templates.

        Returns:
            str: Emoji icon representing the file type.
        """
        if not self.file_extension:
            return '📁'

        icons = {
            'pdf':  '📄',
            'doc':  '📝',
            'docx': '📝',
            'ppt':  '📊',
            'pptx': '📊',
            'xls':  '📈',
            'xlsx': '📈',
            'png':  '🖼️',
            'jpg':  '🖼️',
            'jpeg': '🖼️',
            'gif':  '🖼️',
            'zip':  '📦',
            'rar':  '📦',
            'txt':  '📋',
            'py':   '🐍',
        }
        return icons.get(self.file_extension.lower(), '📁')

    # ==========================================================
    # STATUS MANAGEMENT METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def mark_under_review(self):
        """
        Mark this submission as currently being reviewed
        by an admin. Called when the admin opens the
        submission in the grading interface.
        """
        self.status = SUBMISSION_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW

    def mark_graded(self, score_percent):
        """
        Mark this submission as graded and update the
        denormalized score fields.

        Called automatically when an admin saves a Grade
        record for this submission.

        Args:
            score_percent (float): The final percentage score
                                   awarded by the admin.
                                   Value between 0.0 and 100.0.
        """
        self.is_graded = True
        self.status = SUBMISSION_STATUS_GRADED
        self.score_percent = round(float(score_percent), 2)

    def mark_returned(self):
        """
        Mark this submission as returned to the learner
        for revision. The learner will see feedback
        and can resubmit if the assignment allows it.
        """
        self.status = SUBMISSION_STATUS_RETURNED
        self.is_graded = False

    def flag(self, reason=None):
        """
        Flag this submission for admin attention.

        Args:
            reason (str, optional): The reason for flagging.
                                    Stored in flag_reason field.
        """
        self.is_flagged = True
        if reason:
            self.flag_reason = reason

    def unflag(self):
        """
        Remove the admin flag from this submission
        and clear the flag reason.
        """
        self.is_flagged = False
        self.flag_reason = None

    # ==========================================================
    # LATE DETECTION
    # ==========================================================

    def check_and_set_late_status(self, due_date):
        """
        Check whether this submission was made after the
        assignment due_date and update the is_late flag
        and status accordingly.

        Should be called at the moment of submission
        creation, passing the assignment's due_date.

        Args:
            due_date (datetime or None): The assignment's
                due_date. If None, submission is never late.
        """
        if due_date and datetime.utcnow() > due_date:
            self.is_late = True
            self.status = SUBMISSION_STATUS_LATE

    # ==========================================================
    # DISPLAY HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def get_status_label(self):
        """
        Return a human-readable label for the current
        submission status.

        Returns:
            str: Descriptive status label.
        """
        labels = {
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_SUBMITTED:    'Submitted',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW: 'Under Review',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_GRADED:       'Graded',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_RETURNED:     'Returned for Revision',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_LATE:         'Late Submission',
        }
        return labels.get(self.status, 'Unknown')

    def get_status_badge_class(self):
        """
        Return a CSS class name for the submission status
        badge used in admin and learner templates.

        Returns:
            str: CSS badge class string.
        """
        badge_classes = {
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_SUBMITTED:    'badge-info',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW: 'badge-warning',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_GRADED:       'badge-success',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_RETURNED:     'badge-danger',
            SUBMISSION_STATUS_LATE:         'badge-orange',
        }
        return badge_classes.get(self.status, 'badge-secondary')

    def get_score_display(self):
        """
        Format the score_percent value into a clean
        percentage string for display in templates.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted score string or 'Not graded yet'.

        Examples:
            85.5  → '85.50%'
            100.0 → '100%'
            None  → 'Not graded yet'
        """
        if self.score_percent is None:
            return 'Not graded yet'

        value = float(self.score_percent)
        if value == int(value):
            return f'{int(value)}%'
        return f'{value:.2f}%'

    def get_text_preview(self, max_length=200):
        """
        Generate a truncated preview of the text_content
        for display in submission list views where the
        full text is too long to show.

        Args:
            max_length (int): Maximum number of characters
                              to include in the preview.
                              Default is 200.

        Returns:
            str: Truncated text with ellipsis if needed,
                 or a placeholder if no text content exists.

        Example:
            Long text → 'The soil sample collected from...'
        """
        if not self.text_content:
            return 'No text submitted'

        text = self.text_content.strip()

        if len(text) <= max_length:
            return text

        return text[:max_length].rstrip() + '...'

    def get_submission_type_display(self):
        """
        Return a human-readable description of what type
        of content this submission contains.

        Returns:
            str: Descriptive content type string.

        Examples:
            'Text and File'
            'Text only'
            'File only'
            'Empty'
        """
        if self.has_both():
            return 'Text and File'
        elif self.has_text_content():
            return 'Text only'
        elif self.has_file():
            return 'File only'
        else:
            return 'Empty'

    def get_date_submitted_display(self):
        """
        Format the date_submitted timestamp into a
        human-readable string for display in templates.

        Returns:
            str: Formatted submission date string.

        Example:
            '15 January 2025 at 02:30 PM UTC'
        """
        return self.date_submitted.strftime('%d %B %Y at %I:%M %p UTC')

    def get_days_since_submission(self):
        """
        Calculate the number of days that have passed
        since this submission was made.

        Returns:
            int: Number of days since submission.
        """
        delta = datetime.utcnow() - self.date_submitted
        return delta.days

    # ==========================================================
    # STATIC UTILITY METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    @staticmethod
    def generate_stored_filename(original_filename):
        """
        Generate a unique server-side filename for an
        uploaded submission file by prepending a UUID4
        prefix to the sanitized original filename.

        This prevents filename collisions when multiple
        learners upload files with the same name, and
        eliminates directory traversal vulnerabilities.

        Args:
            original_filename (str): The original filename
                                     as provided by the learner.

        Returns:
            str: UUID-prefixed safe filename string.

        Example:
            'assignment report.pdf' → 'b4e2f1a8_assignment_report.pdf'
        """
        import uuid
        import re

        safe_name = re.sub(r'[^\w\-.]', '_', original_filename)
        unique_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        return f'{unique_id}_{safe_name}'

    @staticmethod
    def get_next_attempt_number(assignment_id, user_id):
        """
        Calculate the next attempt number for a learner
        submitting to a specific assignment.

        Queries existing submissions for this learner and
        assignment, then returns the count + 1.

        Args:
            assignment_id (int): The assignment's primary key.
            user_id (int): The learner's primary key.

        Returns:
            int: The next sequential attempt number.
                 Returns 1 if this is the first submission.

        Example:
            If learner has 2 existing submissions → returns 3
        """
        count = Submission.query.filter_by(
            assignment_id=assignment_id,
            user_id=user_id
        ).count()
        return count + 1

    # ==========================================================
    # SERIALIZATION
    # ==========================================================

    def to_dict(self, include_text=False):
        """
        Serialize the Submission object to a plain dictionary
        suitable for JSON responses and template rendering.

        Args:
            include_text (bool): If True, includes the full
                text_content in the response. Default is False
                to keep list views lightweight — the full text
                is only needed in the detail/grading view.

        Returns:
            dict: Submission data with all computed fields.
        """
        data = {
            'id':                       self.id,
            'user_id':                  self.user_id,
            'assignment_id':            self.assignment_id,
            'attempt_number':           self.attempt_number,
            'has_text_content':         self.has_text_content(),
            'has_file':                 self.has_file(),
            'has_both':                 self.has_both(),
            'submission_type_display':  self.get_submission_type_display(),
            'text_preview':             self.get_text_preview(),
            'file_name':                self.file_name,
            'stored_file_name':         self.stored_file_name,
            'file_extension':           self.file_extension,
            'file_size_bytes':          self.file_size_bytes,
            'file_size_display':        self.get_file_size_display(),
            'file_icon':                self.get_file_icon(),
            'file_url':                 self.get_file_url(),
            'mime_type':                self.mime_type,
            'status':                   self.status,
            'status_label':             self.get_status_label(),
            'status_badge_class':       self.get_status_badge_class(),
            'is_late':                  self.is_late,
            'is_graded':                self.is_graded,
            'score_percent':            float(self.score_percent)
                                        if self.score_percent is not None
                                        else None,
            'score_display':            self.get_score_display(),
            'learner_notes':            self.learner_notes,
            'is_flagged':               self.is_flagged,
            'flag_reason':              self.flag_reason,
            'days_since_submission':    self.get_days_since_submission(),
            'date_submitted':           self.date_submitted.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            'date_submitted_display':   self.get_date_submitted_display(),
            'date_updated':             self.date_updated.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
                                        if self.date_updated else None,
        }

        # Include full text only when explicitly requested
        # Used in the admin grading view and learner detail view
        if include_text:
            data['text_content'] = self.text_content

        # Include grade data if this submission has been graded
        if self.is_graded and self.grade:
            data['grade'] = self.grade.to_dict()
        else:
            data['grade'] = None

        return data

    # ==========================================================
    # STRING REPRESENTATION
    # ==========================================================

    def __repr__(self):
        return (
            f'<Submission id={self.id} '
            f'user_id={self.user_id} '
            f'assignment_id={self.assignment_id} '
            f'attempt={self.attempt_number} '
            f'status={self.status!r} '
            f'graded={self.is_graded}>'
        )

# =============================================================
# Agri LMS — User Model
# =============================================================
# File    : app/models/user.py
# Purpose : Defines the User database model representing all
#           platform users — both learners and administrators.
#           Implements Flask-Login's UserMixin for session
#           management and Werkzeug for password hashing.
#
# Relationships:
#   User ──< Enrollment       (one user enrolls in many courses)
#   User ──< Submission       (one user submits many assignments)
#   User ──< Progress         (one user has many progress records)
#   User ──< Course           (one admin creates many courses)
#   User ──< Assignment       (one admin creates many assignments)
#   User ──< Grade            (one admin grades many submissions)
# =============================================================

from datetime import datetime
from flask_login import UserMixin
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash

from app.extensions import db


# =============================================================
# USER MODEL
# =============================================================

class User(UserMixin, db.Model):
    """
    Represents every registered user on the platform.

    Two roles are supported:
        'learner' — A student who enrolls in and studies courses.
        'admin'   — A platform administrator who manages all
                    content, courses, assignments, and grades.

    Flask-Login integration is provided through UserMixin,
    which supplies the default implementations of:
        is_authenticated, is_active, is_anonymous, get_id()
    """

    __tablename__ = 'users'

    # ── Primary Key ───────────────────────────────────────────
    id = db.Column(
        db.Integer,
        primary_key=True,
        autoincrement=True,
        comment='Unique user identifier — auto-incremented primary key'
    )

    # ── Personal Information ──────────────────────────────────
    full_name = db.Column(
        db.String(150),
        nullable=False,
        comment='Full legal name of the user'
    )

    email = db.Column(
        db.String(150),
        nullable=False,
        unique=True,
        index=True,
        comment='Unique email address — used as login identifier'
    )

    phone_number = db.Column(
        db.String(20),
        nullable=True,
        comment='Optional contact phone number'
    )

    # ── Location ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    state = db.Column(
        db.String(100),
        nullable=True,
        comment='State or province of residence'
    )

    country = db.Column(
        db.String(100),
        nullable=True,
        default='Nigeria',
        comment='Country of residence'
    )

    # ── Profile ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    profile_photo = db.Column(
        db.String(255),
        nullable=True,
        default='default_profile.png',
        comment='Filename of uploaded profile photo stored in static/uploads/profiles/'
    )

    bio = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment='Short biography or personal description of the user'
    )

    farming_background = db.Column(
        db.Text,
        nullable=True,
        comment='Brief description of the user farming experience or agricultural background'
    )

    # ── Authentication ────────────────────────────────────────
    password_hash = db.Column(
        db.String(256),
        nullable=False,
        comment='Werkzeug-hashed password — plaintext is never stored'
    )

    # ── Role-Based Access Control ─────────────────────────────
    role = db.Column(
        db.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default='learner',
        comment='User role — learner: standard student | admin: platform administrator'
    )

    # ── Account Status ────────────────────────────────────────
    is_active = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=True,
        comment='Account active flag — False means the account is suspended'
    )

    email_verified = db.Column(
        db.Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
        comment='Whether the user has verified their email address'
    )

    # ── Timestamps ────────────────────────────────────────────
    date_registered = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=False,
        default=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of when the account was created'
    )

    last_login = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=True,
        comment='UTC timestamp of the most recent successful login'
    )

    date_updated = db.Column(
        db.DateTime,
        nullable=True,
        onupdate=datetime.utcnow,
        comment='UTC timestamp of the last profile update'
    )

    # ── Relationships ─────────────────────────────────────────
    # Courses created by this user (admin only)
    courses_created = db.relationship(
        'Course',
        backref='created_by_user',
        lazy='dynamic',
        foreign_keys='Course.created_by',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # Assignments created by this user (admin only)
    assignments_created = db.relationship(
        'Assignment',
        backref='created_by_user',
        lazy='dynamic',
        foreign_keys='Assignment.created_by',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # Course enrollments for this user (learner only)
    enrollments = db.relationship(
        'Enrollment',
        backref='learner',
        lazy='dynamic',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # Assignment submissions by this user (learner only)
    submissions = db.relationship(
        'Submission',
        backref='learner',
        lazy='dynamic',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # Module progress records for this user (learner only)
    progress_records = db.relationship(
        'Progress',
        backref='learner',
        lazy='dynamic',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # Grades awarded by this user (admin only)
    grades_awarded = db.relationship(
        'Grade',
        backref='graded_by_user',
        lazy='dynamic',
        foreign_keys='Grade.graded_by',
        cascade='all, delete-orphan'
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # PASSWORD METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def set_password(self, password):
        """
        Hash and store the provided plaintext password.
        Uses Werkzeug's pbkdf2:sha256 hashing algorithm.

        Args:
            password (str): Plaintext password from registration
                            or password change form.

        Example:
            user.set_password('MySecurePassword123')
        """
        self.password_hash = generate_password_hash(password)

    def check_password(self, password):
        """
        Verify a plaintext password against the stored hash.

        Args:
            password (str): Plaintext password from login form.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the password matches, False otherwise.

        Example:
            if user.check_password('MySecurePassword123'):
                login_user(user)
        """
        return check_password_hash(self.password_hash, password)

    # ==========================================================
    # ROLE HELPER METHODS
    # ==========================================================

    def is_admin(self):
        """
        Check whether this user has the administrator role.

        Returns:
            bool: True if role is 'admin', False otherwise.
        """
        return self.role == 'admin'

    def is_learner(self):
        """
        Check whether this user has the learner role.

        Returns:
            bool: True if role is 'learner', False otherwise.
        """
        return self.role == 'learner'

    # ==========================================================
    # FLASK-LOGIN REQUIRED OVERRIDE
    # ==========================================================

    def get_id(self):
        """
        Return the user's primary key as a string.
        Required by Flask-Login for session management.

        Returns:
            str: String representation of the user's integer ID.
        """
        return str(self.id)

    # ==========================================================
    # ENROLLMENT HELPERS
    # ==========================================================

    def is_enrolled_in(self, course_id):
        """
        Check whether this learner is enrolled in a given course.

        Args:
            course_id (int): The primary key of the course to check.

        Returns:
            bool: True if an active enrollment exists.
        """
        from app.models.enrollment import Enrollment
        return self.enrollments.filter_by(
            course_id=course_id,
            is_active=True
        ).first() is not None

    def get_enrollment(self, course_id):
        """
        Retrieve the Enrollment object for a specific course.

        Args:
            course_id (int): The primary key of the course.

        Returns:
            Enrollment or None: The enrollment record if found.
        """
        from app.models.enrollment import Enrollment
        return self.enrollments.filter_by(
            course_id=course_id
        ).first()

    def total_enrollments(self):
        """
        Count the total number of courses this learner
        has enrolled in.

        Returns:
            int: Total enrollment count.
        """
        return self.enrollments.count()

    def completed_courses(self):
        """
        Count the number of courses this learner has completed.

        Returns:
            int: Number of completed enrollments.
        """
        from app.models.enrollment import Enrollment
        return self.enrollments.filter_by(
            is_completed=True
        ).count()

    # ==========================================================
    # SERIALIZATION
    # ==========================================================

    def to_dict(self):
        """
        Serialize the User object to a plain dictionary.
        The password hash is deliberately excluded for security.

        Returns:
            dict: User data safe for JSON responses or template use.
        """
        return {
            'id':                 self.id,
            'full_name':          self.full_name,
            'email':              self.email,
            'phone_number':       self.phone_number,
            'state':              self.state,
            'country':            self.country,
            'profile_photo':      self.profile_photo,
            'bio':                self.bio,
            'farming_background': self.farming_background,
            'role':               self.role,
            'is_active':          self.is_active,
            'email_verified':     self.email_verified,
            'date_registered':    self.date_registered.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
            'last_login':         self.last_login.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
                                  if self.last_login else None,
        }

    # ==========================================================
    # STRING REPRESENTATION
    # ==========================================================

    def __repr__(self):
        return (
            f'<User id={self.id} '
            f'email={self.email!r} '
            f'role={self.role!r}>'
        )

admin_bp = Blueprint('admin', __name__)


def admin_required(f):
    """Restrict access to admin users only."""
    @wraps(f)
    def decorated(*args, **kwargs):
        if not current_user.is_admin():
            flash('Administrator privileges required.', 'error')
            return redirect(url_for('learner.dashboard'))
        return f(*args, **kwargs)
    return decorated
